trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied AST is well typed enough for its values to be written into generated JavaScript. At the pinned commit this is decided once, in the parser entry (validateInputAst, keyed on node.type and checking only PathExpression depth/parts and Number/Boolean literal values). The fix moves the decision to the compiler handlers that emit each value.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'bypass of CVE-2026-33937, AST type confusion in compile'. The earlier fix's validator sits here, and the existing tests (spec/security.js:447-504) point at it. The obvious move is to extend this walker.

fix_sites.entry_point: Handlebars.parse / parseWithoutProcessing / compile / precompile (removal of the parser-level validator)
Handlebars.compile / precompile with an AST whose Program.blockParams is not an array; the length reaches container.program(...) at lib/handlebars/compiler/javascript-compiler.js:959-970
fix_sites.module_kind: compiler visitor -> code generator in another file

fix_sites.entry_point: Handlebars.compile / precompile (PathExpression depth/parts; lookupData depth at lib/handlebars/compiler/javascript-compiler.js:526-531)
Handlebars.compile / precompile (helper name from parts[0], read before the PathExpression handler runs)
Handlebars.compile(ast, {stringParams:true}) and {trackIds:true}: param value/original/depth of any node type
helper call on an AST without loc (options.loc)
error construction for nodes with partial loc

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/handlebars.js:28 exports Handlebars.Compiler (lib/handlebars/compiler/compiler.js:50). Calling it directly never runs the parse-time validator at lib/handlebars/compiler/base.js:17. Second spot: the option-mode branches stringParams/trackIds at lib/handlebars/compiler/compiler.js:414-450, which emit through lib/handlebars/compiler/javascript-compiler.js:601-605 and 1107-1112

O3_reason_to_dismiss: stringParams/trackIds are legacy Ember-era options and docs/compiler-api.md:7 only promises AST input to compile/precompile. A solver can argue that extending the parser walker for the default mode is enough, and that direct Handlebars.Compiler use and the option modes are unsupported combinations.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Hand-built ASTs that omit depth must compile with depth treated as 0; the pinned validator rejects these at lib/handlebars/compiler/base.js:59,94-100. Very long number literals that the parser turns into Infinity must still compile, so a strict isFinite check moved into the NumberLiteral handler breaks string templates. ASTs without loc must still invoke helpers (also in strict mode). In stringParams mode, '../' stripping of path originals must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: string where number/boolean expected (NumberLiteral.value, BooleanLiteral.value, depth '0')
object with a forged length (Program.blockParams: {length: code})
value/original on a non-literal node (PathExpression) in stringParams mode
depth on a non-PathExpression param in stringParams mode

O7_producer.where: The caller builds the AST, and the project has no in-repo schema or serializer for it. The pinned check (lib/handlebars/compiler/base.js:44-92) dispatches on the declared node.type, but the consumer pushParam (lib/handlebars/compiler/compiler.js:412,419-423) reads value/original/depth from any node type. That is a how-type differential, not a producer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: partial indent emitted by string concatenation instead of JSON.stringify (indent comes from lib/handlebars/compiler/compiler.js:195)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Other options in the same object literal are raw code strings ('helpers', 'partials'), so a maintainer could easily wrap indent in quotes by hand.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: decorator param count or a new decorator option taken from the AST and interpolated in registerDecorator (lib/handlebars/compiler/javascript-compiler.js:685-707)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Decorators are a separate, rarely used code path; the fix never touches DecoratorBlock.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second depth consumer (e.g. a compat-mode depthedLookup variant taking depth from opcode args) that is not fed through validateDepth
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: lookupData already concatenates depth into code. The code comment says javascript-compiler.js trusts opcode args, so any new opcode arg taken from the AST is a sibling.

O9_family: code injection via AST type confusion in a template-to-JavaScript compiler (CWE-843 -> CWE-94)

O10_build.project_tests: spec/security.js:447-504 (untrusted AST inputs), spec/compiler.js AST rejection tests; run via npm test (mocha)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add StringLiteral and blockParams checks to the existing validateAstNode walker in base.js, keyed on node.type. That leaves depth/value on other node types in stringParams mode, direct Handlebars.Compiler use, and the missing-depth/Infinity regressions.

out_of_scope_notes: Compiler.accept dispatches on this[node.type]; Object.prototype names such as 'constructor' resolve to a handler (lib/handlebars/compiler/compiler.js:93-98). Looks like a crash/no-op, not injection; not pursued.
The runtime compiles AST-valued registered partials at render time (lib/handlebars/runtime.js:82-87). This funnels into the same compile(), so the compiler-level fix covers it.
